title: Maths from zero: little numbers, big ideas

lessons.objective: Count each object once and give an empty pile its number.
Bundle ten counters and see what each digit means.
Join two piles and discover what the plus sign means.
Remove counters and check what is left.
Connect equal groups to a multiplication fact.
Share equal amounts and explain what is left over.
Explain a square number with equal rows and columns, then spot the odd-number gaps.
Identify prime and composite numbers by their different positive factors, and explain why 1 is neither.

OpenStax — Prealgebra 2e: Find Multiples and Factors

glossary.definition: Put amounts together to find a total.
Find what remains when an amount is taken away.
Groups that each contain the same amount.
The number we use for none.
The result of multiplying a whole number by itself.
A whole number that divides another whole number exactly, with no remainder.
A whole number greater than 1 with exactly two different positive factors: 1 and itself.

outcomes: Read two-digit numbers as tens and ones.
Model addition with two small piles.
Model subtraction and check it by adding.
Share whole objects equally and identify a remainder.
Read squared notation and connect whole-number squares to tile arrangements.
Count different positive factors to distinguish primes, composites and the number 1.
description: Eight short maths lessons: count, add, subtract, make equal groups, explore squares and discover why prime numbers have just two factors. Optional quizzes included.
introduction:
Begin with a small pile of counters and an empty space. Learn to count, build tens, add, subtract and share equally. Then grow a square and discover which numbers refuse to form equal groups.

Each short lesson adds one idea. Read at your own pace; optional quizzes stay tucked away until you want them.
prerequisites: No arithmetic background. Start by counting the counters one at a time.
